topic: Brand love, churn, and AI-powered CX
angle: Use AI to earn ‘brand love’ by fixing journeys that actually drive churn—and prove it with hard metrics.
sourceTitle: AT&T’s CMO tied ‘brand love’ to the numbers CEOs care about. Customers are 3 times less likely to leave and much cheaper to acquire
linkedinPost:
“Brand love” only matters if it moves the numbers CEOs care about.

Fortune reports AT&T customers who love the brand are 3x less likely to leave, 50% more likely to buy a second product, and cheaper to acquire. That’s not squishy—it’s a retention and CAC story.

My take: AI should be pointed at the parts of the journey that create or destroy that love—billing confusion, slow support, opaque offers—not at vanity experiences.

How to make it real:
- Map top 5 churn drivers, then deploy AI to prevent them (proactive outreach, next-best-action, clearer language).
- Measure lift with hard metrics: voluntary churn, save rate, time-to-resolution, and incremental products per customer.
- Close the loop: when AI resolves the issue, ask for a micro-review or NPS—tie signals back to churn cohorts.

If your AI roadmap can’t show a line from a specific journey fix to reduced churn or higher attach, it’s not CX—it’s theater.

Where have you used AI to cut a measurable point of churn? #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption
